key_facts: **Bimatoprost** is a prostamide (glaucoma drug) that lengthens, thickens and darkens eyelashes when applied to the upper lid margin.
Works by **prolonging anagen**; results build over weeks to months and reverse on stopping.
Warn about **permanent iris darkening** (hazel/green eyes), reversible eyelid pigmentation, irritation and redness.
Exclude a disease cause of lash loss (alopecia areata, thyroid disease, blepharitis, trichotillomania).
Cosmetic serums vary in content; prescription products need proper counselling.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: **Eyelash enhancement** options include cosmetics, lifts and **bimatoprost** (a prostamide also used in glaucoma drops) applied to the upper lid margin to lengthen lashes.

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: Bimatoprost increases eyelash length, thickness and darkness by **extending anagen** and stimulating follicle melanogenesis; periocular skin and iris melanocytes can also respond.

ul: **"Natural serums are safer"**: many contain undeclared prostaglandin analogues.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: Bimatoprost acts on **prostamide receptors** in the lash follicle to keep it growing.

mech.t: Bimatoprost binds prostamide/FP receptors in the dermal papilla.
Follicles stay in the growth phase longer and more follicles enter anagen.
Iris and eyelid melanocytes increase pigment production.

ul: Longer, darker lashes over weeks to months.
Side effects: periocular hyperpigmentation, **iris colour change** (especially hazel/green eyes), itch, redness; periorbital fat atrophy (glaucoma-dose context).

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Before use: exclude a disease cause of sparse lashes (**madarosis**): alopecia areata, thyroid disease, blepharitis, trichotillomania, chemotherapy.

head: Cause of sparse lashes
Clue
rows: Loss of the outer brows; systemic symptoms

ul: Explain cosmetic versus glaucoma origins; apply only as directed to the upper lid margin, not into the eye for cosmetic use.
Warn about **permanent iris darkening**, reversible periocular skin darkening, possible hair growth on unintended skin if the product migrates, and ocular irritation.
Avoid with active ocular inflammation unless an ophthalmologist agrees; remove contact lenses as per product advice.
Effects reverse over weeks to months if stopped.
Check the current SmPC/BNF; this page does not cover off-label periocular protocols.

drugs.name: Bimatoprost (eyelash)
drugs.cautions: Permanent iris darkening possible; periocular pigment reverses.

ladder.t: Check for alopecia areata, blepharitis, thyroid disease, trichotillomania.

refer.t: Lash loss with scalp or brow loss, or lid disease: GP/dermatology/ophthalmology.
Eye pain, redness or visual change on treatment.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Eye pain, redness or visual change: stop and seek ophthalmology review.
Patients on glaucoma drops: discuss with their ophthalmologist (additive effect on intraocular pressure).
Iris pigmentation (permanent), periocular pigmentation, conjunctival hyperaemia, periorbital fat atrophy.
Lashes return to baseline within weeks to months after stopping.

pearls: Eyelash serums sold cosmetically vary widely; prescription bimatoprost needs proper counselling on iris pigment.

quiz.a: Periocular skin darkening and the lash growth.
Loss of eyelashes or eyebrows, which may signal disease.
